title: Cohen's d and Distributional Overlap
summary: The learner estimates on a slider what share of two distributions overlaps at a conventionally large effect before anything is revealed, and almost always guesses far too little. The explorer then draws two normal distributions with the common ground shaded and reports four descriptions of the same gap side by side: Cohen's d, the overlap coefficient, the probability of superiority and U3. Group spreads can be pulled apart, so the pooled standard deviation becomes visible arithmetic and the overlap has to be integrated rather than read off the equal-variance formula, and a sample-size slider moves the t statistic and the p-value across orders of magnitude while the effect size refuses to move at all.
learningObjectives: Compute Cohen's d from a mean difference and a pooled standard deviation and explain why it has no units.
Translate an effect size into overlap, probability of superiority and U3.
Explain why the same raw difference gives different effect sizes in groups of different spread.
Explain why the sample size changes a test statistic but not an effect size.
State what a group difference does and does not license about an individual.
interactionTypes: unequal group spreads with a visible pooled figure
sample-size slider that cannot move the effect
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; every value is computed in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native ranges, selects and buttons, each with an explicit label and grouped in a fieldset with a legend; the estimate slider announces 'an estimated overlap of 30 per cent' and the sample-size slider says in words that it changes the test and not the effect size. The chart is hidden from assistive technology and paired inside its figure with a visible three-column table naming each index, its value and what it counts, and a disclosure holds a second table showing which quantities move with the sample size and which do not. Group A is a solid line and group B dashed, both are named at their own peaks, each mean is a dotted rule, and the shaded common ground carries a vertical hatch, so nothing depends on colour. The pinned primary result measures 514px tall at 1366x768. Every preset and slider announces a full sentence through the polite live region, focus moves to the explorer heading when it opens, forced-colours rules are provided, and the layout is usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths with no horizontal page scroll.
readmeTopic: A conventionally large effect still leaves two thirds of the two distributions overlapping
simulationNotes: No data are generated: both groups are mathematical normal distributions on an invented 100-point scale, with group A fixed at a mean of 50. The pooled standard deviation is the root mean square of the two group standard deviations, since group sizes are equal, and Cohen's d is the mean difference divided by it. The overlap coefficient is integrated numerically - a trapezoidal sum of the minimum of the two densities over two thousand steps across the plotted range - rather than taken from the closed form 2*Phi(-|d|/2), because that form is only correct when the two standard deviations are equal and this tool deliberately lets them differ. The probability of superiority is Phi of the mean difference over the root of the summed variances, which stays exact under unequal variances, and U3 is defined as the share of group B above group A's mean, Phi of the mean difference over group B's standard deviation. The sample-size slider feeds only a two-sample t statistic, mean difference over pooled SD times the root of two over n on 2n-2 degrees of freedom, with a two-tailed p from the regularised incomplete beta function; at d = 0.80 it runs from t = 1.79, p = .090 at ten per group to t = 11.31, p below .0001 at four hundred, with the effect size and overlap unchanged. Every index describes two distributions and none describes a person, which the page states repeatedly. Cohen's small, medium and large labels are printed with the caveat he attached to them himself.
